extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners; patent practitioners (attorneys/agents) and applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural standards for examination of U.S. patent applications (MPEP Chapter 700), including statutory bases, requisites for applications, search and information requirements, rejections, interviews, affidavits, petitions, and handling of confidential materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory Authority for Examination (35 U.S.C. 131; 35 U.S.C. 101)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall cause an examination to be made of the application and the alleged new invention; and if on such examination it appears that the applicant is entitled to a patent under the law, the Director shall issue a patent therefor. The main conditions precedent to the grant of a patent to an applicant are set forth in 35 U.S.C. 101, 102 and 103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 7.04 copies 35 U.S.C. 101. Use statutory bases (35 U.S.C. 101, 102, 103) as primary criteria for patentability determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requisites of the Application (35 U.S.C. 111(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: When a new application is assigned in the Technology Center, the examiner should review the contents of the application to determine if the application meets the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 111(a). Matters affecting filing date or abandonment, such as lack of an oath/declaration, filing fee, or claims should be checked. The examiner should see that the application meets all requisites as to formal matters and completeness and clarity of disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requisites are not met, applicant may be called upon for necessary amendments, but such amendments must not include new matter. See MPEP Chapter 600 for formal matters. For Image File Wrapper (IFW) processing, see IFW Manual sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obviously Informal Cases — examiner procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application is impractical for complete action on the merits due to informal or insufficient disclosure, follow a limited procedure: make a reasonable search (unless disclosure is incomprehensible); point out informalities and drawing deficiencies; require specification revision to idiomatic English and U.S. patent practice; reject informal claims under 35 U.S.C. 112 (blanket rejection usually sufficient).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attempt to point out specific points of informality. Treat a number of obviously informal claims as a single claim for fee and examination purposes. Applicants are urged to submit a preliminary amendment (preferably within 3 months) correcting informalities; preliminary amendments must not add new matter. Use form paragraph 7.01 or 7.02 when a proper search cannot be made due to unconventional terminology or incomprehensible disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search — examiner must search prior art (MPEP § 704.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: After reading the specification and claims, the examiner searches the prior art. The invention should be thoroughly understood before a search is undertaken. Informal cases also receive a search to avoid piecemeal prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give full faith and credit to prior examiner’s search/action unless clear error or knowledge of other prior art exists; generally do not reorient the approach merely to attempt to find something new. See MPEP Chapter 900 (esp. §§ 904–904.03) for search procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for Information under 37 CFR 1.105
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner or other Office employee may require from inventors (and certain assignees) the submission of such information as may be reasonably necessary to properly examine or treat the matter in a pending or abandoned application, patent, or reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include: commercial databases known to inventors that could be searched; whether a prior art search was made and what was searched; copies of non-patent literature/published applications/patents related to the claimed invention; information used to draft the application or during invention process; identification of improvements; identification of any use of the claimed invention known to inventors at filing; technical information known to applicant pertinent to patentability or to the examiner’s interpretation. Requirements may be presented as factual requirements, interrogatories, or stipulations. Replies stating information is unknown or not readily available may be accepted as complete replies. Requirements may be included in Office action or sent separately; replies governed by §§ 1.135 and 1.136.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and Standard for Making a Requirement for Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Information required under 37 CFR 1.105 must be reasonably necessary to properly examine or treat the matter and there must be a reasonable basis for the information required. The requirement places a substantial burden on the applicant and should be narrowly focused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The terms 'factual' and 'facts' mean factual information known to applicant or readily obtained after reasonable inquiry; requirements are not for opinions. Applicant need not derive facts by new experimentation. The purpose is to improve patent quality and decision-making, not to jeopardize duties of candor. Examiner must have reasonable basis for requiring the information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of Information Reasonably Required (illustrative list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific examples of information that may be reasonably required include: name/citation of particularly relevant indexed journal or treatise; trade name of goods/services embodying claimed subject matter; citations/dates/copies of advertising/promotional literature; journal articles describing goods/services; trade names/providers of competing goods/services; written descriptions/analyses prepared by inventors or assignees; identification of pending/abandoned applications by inventor/assignee disclosing similar subject matter; replies to protests; explanation of technical material in a publication; identification of changes made in reformatted continuing applications; CIP mark-ups showing added subject matter; comments on new Federal Circuit decisions; publication date of undated documents; information bearing on derivation (35 U.S.C. 102(f)); and other art or factual information pertinent to patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This list is illustrative, not exhaustive. A requirement for such information is justified when necessary to find prior art or resolve issues arising from the examiner’s search or analysis. The examiner must still perform a search per MPEP § 704.01; a requirement for information is not a substitute for the examiner’s search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interrogatories or Stipulations that may be required
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner may require interrogatories or stipulations seeking applicant’s factual knowledge about matters such as: common technical features among claims; admissions that certain claim groups lack common technical features; support in the disclosure for means- or steps-plus-function claim limitations; identification of portions of the disclosure that provide written description and enablement for specific claim elements; meanings of claim terms or which prior art teachings would be covered by claim limitations; which claim portions correspond to any admitted prior art; specific utility provided by claimed subject matter on a claim-by-claim basis; whether a dependent claim element is known in the prior art; support for added limitations in an amended claim; facts related to public use or sale situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interrogatories/stipulations should seek factual information, and may be required in a focused manner when reasonably necessary. Responses may be accepted as complete if applicant states information is unknown or not readily available.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to Make a Requirement for Information (timing and discretion)
rubrics_metrics.description: A requirement under 37 CFR 1.105 is discretionary and may be made at any time once necessity is recognized. The best time is prior to or with the first action on the merits, because examiner has maximum opportunity to consider and apply the response; ordinarily, a request should not be made with or after a final rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It may be appropriate prior to first action (e.g., restriction requirement, new technology area without adequate classification), with the first action when the file or lack of relevant prior art justifies asking the applicant, or after the first action in rare situations where the file justifies additional applicant information. Consider factors such as whether claimed subject matter is in a newly established art area, whether an IDS was submitted, adequacy of background description, discovery of related documents authored by inventors that were not submitted, references to non-patent literature without supplied copies, or background admissions unfamiliar to examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Form Paragraphs for Unconventional Terminology or Incomprehensible Disclosure (Form ¶ 7.01 & 7.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use form paragraph 7.01 when terminology is so different from art-accepted terminology that a proper search cannot be made; use form paragraph 7.02 where the application is so incomprehensible that a reasonable search cannot be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraphs require applicant to clarify terminology or submit an amendment to clarify disclosure without adding new matter. A shortened statutory period for reply (ONE MONTH or THIRTY DAYS, whichever is longer) is typically set. Examiner notes instruct what to fill in (e.g., bracketed items indicate terminology, pages involved). For drawing informality, see MPEP §§ 608.02(a) and 608.02(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship of Requirement for Information to Duty of Disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: A requirement for information under 37 CFR 1.105 is related to, but distinct from, the applicant’s duty of disclosure; it seeks factual information reasonably necessary to examination and may be directed to inventors and certain assignees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The scope extends to assignees because they may know information inventors do not. Replies stating information is unknown or not readily available may be accepted. Purpose is to improve patent quality; examiners should clearly focus the reason and scope to minimize applicant burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements May Be Presented in Various Forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for factual information may be presented as a requirement for factual information, as interrogatories (specific questions seeking applicant factual knowledge), or as stipulations which applicant may agree or disagree with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the appropriate form to obtain needed factual material; be narrow and specific in scope. See 37 CFR 1.105(a)(3) examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s Obligation Following Applicant’s Reply to Requirements for Information
rubrics_metrics.description: After applicant replies to a requirement for information, the examiner has obligations to consider the reply in the examination and proceed accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replies governed by §§ 1.135 and 1.136. Examiner must review reply for completeness, respond in the next Office action and apply any new information to the examination. (Header present: 'Examiner’s Obligation Following Applicant’s Reply' — see full MPEP for procedural specifics.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability Reports — instructions and use
rubrics_metrics.description: Patentability Reports (P.R.) are prepared and used according to instructions covering nature of P.R., its use and disposal, sequence of examination, counting and recording, duplicate prints of drawings, and limitation as to use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: P.R. utilization is limited as described in MPEP § 705.01 and related subparagraphs. See MPEP §§ 705–705.01 for implementation details (nature, counting, limitations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejections Under 35 U.S.C. 102, 103, 101, 112 and Related Form Paragraphs
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for making rejections under sections 102 (novelty), 103 (obviousness), 101 (statutory subject matter), and 112 (written description and claim definiteness), including contrasts with objections, printed publications or patents, provisional rejections, and various subparts and form paragraphs for use in rejections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed subsections (e.g., 706.02 through 706.07) provide specific handling for each statutory basis, including examination guidelines for references under 102(e), provisional rejections when reference is copending, rejections under 102(f)/(g)/(d)/(c), form paragraphs for 102 rejections, contents of a 103 rejection, provisional rejections combining 102(e)/103, biotechnology process applications (35 U.S.C. 103(b)), rejections not based on prior art, rejections after allowance, final rejections and their proper timing, and treatment of duplicate claims, new matter, disclaimers, reissue, res judicata, etc. Use the appropriate form paragraphs and follow procedural rules for final rejections, withdrawals, RCE practice, and after-final practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews with Applicants — policy and record
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews are governed by general policy (how conducted), interviews prior to first action on the merits, prohibition against interviews for 'sounding out' the examiner, requirement that substance of interview must be made of record, special situations where interviews prohibited or granted, and rules about not discussing inter partes questions ex parte.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document the substance of interviews in the record. Be careful about exposing other cases. Demonstrations, exhibits, models and interviews in finally rejected applications have special handling. See MPEP § 713 and subparts for detailed procedures and restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s Letter or Action — completeness and clarity requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner’s Office action must be complete and clear: indicate all outstanding requirements, complete action on formal matters, use proper language in rejecting claims, answer all material traversed, avoid piecemeal examination, notify of inaccuracies in amendments, mention each claim in each action, state when claims are allowable, number paragraphs, comment on examples, and ensure reviewing and initialing by assistant examiner and signing by authorized examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow internal procedures for entry, dating, mailing returned office action. Use appropriate form paragraphs (MPEP § 707 et seq.). Ensure draftsman requirements and that examiner notes and citations are complete. See detailed subsections for use of form paragraphs and examiner notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of Examination and Special Case Handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination should follow order of examination policies, including lists of special cases, petitions to make special, handling examiner resignations, suspension of action, overlapping applications by same applicant or same assignee, and periods for reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply special procedures for prioritized or special-status cases; manage overlapping applications consistent with guidance in MPEP § 709 and related sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period for Reply — computation and shortened statutory periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory period for reply is computed per rules; shortened statutory periods and specified time limits are available in certain situations. There are differences between shortened statutory periods for reply and specified time limits; provisions for extensions of time apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shortened statutory period is used in specific situations (e.g., when terminology prevents a proper search — form paragraphs 7.01/7.02 set a shortened period of one month/30 days). See MPEP §§ 710–710.06 for computation rules, extension procedures, and situations when reply periods reset or restart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment of Patent Application — grounds and revival
rubrics_metrics.description: Abandonment can be express or formal, including failure to take required action during statutory period or insufficiency of reply. Special situations involve abandonment; procedures for termination of proceedings, reconsideration of holdings of abandonment, revival, petitions relating to abandonment, and examiner’s statement on petition to set aside abandonment exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish holdings based on insufficiency of reply from failure to reply within period. Applicant may petition for revival; public access to abandoned applications and handling (pulling/forwarding) is described. See MPEP § 711 and subsections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavits/Declarations to Disqualify References; Swearing Back (37 CFR 1.131 & 1.132)
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits or declarations may be used to disqualify a commonly owned patent or published application as prior art (swearing back) under 37 CFR 1.130/1.131; guidance on how much of the claimed invention must be shown (including rules for generic claims), genus-species practice when predictability is in question, who may make affidavits/declarations, and formal requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include documentary evidence and testimony where appropriate. Consider interference testimony sometimes used. Diligence, acts relied upon, geographic limits (this country or NAFTA/WTO member countries), disposition of exhibits, and review for evidence of prior public use, sale, or failure to disclose best mode are required. Examiner passes on affidavits for sufficiency and seasonable presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavits/Declarations Traversing Rejections — Objective Evidence of Nonobviousness
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits or declarations (37 CFR 1.132) that traverse rejections must address generally applicable criteria: objective evidence of nonobviousness, nexus requirement and evidence, probative value and weighing of objective evidence, unexpected results, comparison with closest prior art, advantages disclosed or inherent, and proper affidavit/declaration form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objective evidence must show unexpected results commensurate in scope with the claimed invention; burden lies with applicant to provide probative evidence and nexus where needed. Examiner weighs expected vs. alleged unexpected results and considers commercial success, long-felt need, copying, skepticism of experts, and inoperability of references. See MPEP §§ 716–716.03 and subparts for evaluation details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial Success and Other Secondary Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercial success must be commensurate in scope with the claimed invention and derived from the claimed invention. Secondary considerations include long-felt need and failure of others, skepticism of experts, copying, and attribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating commercial success, examiner considers whether success is due to claimed invention, scope alignment, market evidence, and other factors indicating nexus between claimed features and success. Treat as part of overall nonobviousness analysis (see MPEP § 716.03 and following).

rubrics_metrics.name: File Wrapper Contents and Organization; Public Use Proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers in the file wrapper must be organized: arrangement of papers, prints, data entered, changes of inventor name or title, classification during examination, index of claims, field of search, foreign filing dates, related applications, public use proceedings, preliminary handling, examiner determination of prima facie showing, preliminary hearings, public use proceeding testimony, and final decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain completeness of the patent file wrapper and follow record-keeping instructions. Public use proceedings and testimony require special handling. See MPEP § 724 and related sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade Secret, Proprietary, and Protective Order Materials — submission and handling (MPEP § 724.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for submitting trade secret, proprietary, and/or protective order materials under MPEP § 724.02, types of materials, office treatment and handling, and distinctions for materials submitted in applications covered by 35 U.S.C. 122, reissue applications, and reexamination files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow types and methods prescribed for submission (e.g., sealed envelopes, labeling), and office will treat such materials consistent with public access rules (37 CFR 1.11). Materials submitted under § 724.02 have specified handling; failure to properly identify materials (trade secret/proprietary/protective order) may cause their inclusion in prior art search files and could make them irretrievable; take precautions for IFW processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to Expunge Information or Copy of Papers in Application File (37 CFR 1.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: Information in an application will not be expunged except as provided. Information forming part of the original disclosure (specification, claims, drawings, preliminary amendments specifically incorporated in an executed oath/declaration) will not be expunged. An applicant may request expungement (37 CFR 1.59(b)) for information other than original disclosure by petition and fee, establishing to the Director that expungement is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expungement of material originally submitted under MPEP § 724.02 or in an IDS is appropriate if petitioner complies with conditions (items A–E in MPEP § 724.05) and examiner or appropriate official determines information is not material to a reasonable examiner's decision of patentability. If unintentionally submitted, petition may request return rather than transfer. Petitions requiring waiver of 1.59(a) must be filed under 37 CFR 1.183 and directed to Office of Petitions. Decisions often held in abeyance until allowance, Ex parte Quayle action, or abandonment; use form paragraphs (7.204–7.213, 7.205–7.213) to grant/dismiss and to explain deficiencies (lack of fee, failure to show trade secret/proprietary/unintentional submission, failure to commit to retain expunged material, unclear identification of material, not submitted by or on behalf of original submitter, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of Petitions to Expunge — decision standards and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: When deciding petitions to expunge under 37 CFR 1.59(b), the decision may be held in abeyance until the application is allowed or an Ex parte Quayle action or Notice of Abandonment is mailed; at that time, a Technology Center Director decides whether information is material. Petitions must include required fee and show appropriate grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If information was submitted inadvertently, factors in MPEP § 724.05 paragraph II (items A–F) guide grant of petition. If information was submitted in wrong application, Office may transfer without a petition if identification allows. Use form paragraphs to notify petitioner and for decisions. If petition granted, applicant must retain expunged materials for life of any resulting patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Submitted in Incorrect Application — transfer vs expungement
rubrics_metrics.description: When information has been placed in the wrong application due to incorrect heading, petitioner should request expungement rather than transfer; however, if the Office can determine the correct intended application based on identifying information in the heading, the Office will transfer the papers to the correct file without a petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use petition when appropriate; IFW processing considerations apply. If information is clearly in wrong application, do not hold decision in abeyance unnecessarily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraphs and Templates for Common Actions (numerous ¶ 7.xxx)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use prescribed form paragraphs and templates (e.g., ¶ 7.01, 7.02, 7.204–7.213, 7.205–7.213, etc.) for standard communications: notices of incomprehensible disclosure, use of unconventional terminology, petitions to expunge (held in abeyance, granted, dismissed), and many other routine examiner statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fill bracketed fields in form paragraphs with particularized information (e.g., pages, items not understood, document titles). Follow examiner notes for correct selection and usage of form paragraphs. Ensure proper mailing and cover sheets (PTO-90C) when required.
